title: Raise upstream: the Claude Code harness's worktree isolation refuses a git probe
why: Lane session_013NEJKzXJPDWrSRe3i1fGJd (#1593) met a refusal whose text comes from the Claude Code harness's worktree isolation, not from a claude-settings guard: a grep of main finds nothing (coordinator, 04:44 CST Nov 8).
note: Fix: none — the refusal text is the Claude Code harness's worktree isolation, not a claude-settings guard (grep of main finds nothing). Until: 2026-11-21. Raise it upstream. Filed 04:46 CST Nov 8. False-alarm sighting (lane git-dash-c-other-checkout, #2323, via the coordinator 17:16 CST Nov 8): the harness worktree check counts "git" inside a branch name as a second git call, so it refuses `git push origin HEAD:git-dash-c-other-checkout`. Sighting (lane encoded-retry-after-refusal, session_013NEJL37B9ZSA9toGnPeeVa, 17:28 CST Nov 8): in a session isolated in a worktree (EnterWorktree, .claude/worktrees/encoded-retry-merge), the harness refused three plain commands as "too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree": `python3 merge/merge.py --lane-lint 2314` (one command, worktree root, nothing chained), `~/.claude/bin/verdict ~/.claude/bin/merge --lane-lint 2314`, and the same after a cd into the worktree. The command names no git call; the merge tool runs git inside. The same command ran from the main checkout.
